target_customer: Gamers (consumers) and game publishers; later streamers and viewers who buy clip NFTs
problem: Players grind challenges in many games with no cross-game reward. Later, streamers had no way for fans to own and trade the best moments of a stream.
business_model: Cross-game battle pass subscription, then NFT marketplace take rate on streamer clips
product_category: Gaming rewards, then NFT marketplace for streaming clips

founders.name: Derek Chiang
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CTO by Crunchbase via search summaries; the YC page lists only Tong.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed game API integrations across seven titles with a three person team, plus stats tracking. Later work on a blockchain marketplace on Flow was standard but new.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on game developers' data access, which could be revoked, and rewards logic was copyable. NFT marketplace had no clear moat beyond streamer relationships.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Publishers run their own battle passes inside each game. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Zelos.

market_need_then: In early 2020 battle passes were a proven monetization format inside single games (Fortnite, Apex) and players showed strong demand for challenges. Demand for a cross-game version was unproven.

rebrands.why: Not stated; product pivoted to a clip NFT marketplace branded Eternal.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself. Zelos is a Greek word for zeal (a dictionary meaning, not a stated origin) and is shared with a game character and other companies. Eternal got launch press in 2021 but no sign of a lasting brand.

pivots.to: Eternal, an NFT marketplace for Twitch streamer clips

outcome_analysis: Zelos launched a cross-game battle pass in 2020 that relied on game developers' data access, then pivoted to Eternal, an NFT marketplace for Twitch clips, and raised a reported 4.5 million dollar seed in September 2021 from crypto and angel backers. The YC directory marks it as acquired but no acquirer or date was found, and one aggregator hints at a wind down around late 2022 after the NFT market cooled. The cause and deal terms are not public.
notes: Website eternal.gg returned HTTP 503 when fetched. Acquirer and date not found; exit type follows YC status. The 4.5M seed is in the TechCrunch story headline context and CoinCarp (Sep 28, 2021, 22 investors). Aggregators conflict: CB Insights total 3.15M, StartupIntros lists 300K (Mar 2020) and 1M (Oct 2019), and TechCrunch Apr 2020 says Tong reportedly raised 2.8M after demo day; all unverified. No dated direct competitor named in the April 2020 coverage, so the list is empty.
